blocks.value: To prevent extreme price movements in a single day, stock exchanges impose price limits called Upper Circuit and Lower Circuit.
Imagine This: Roads have speed limits to prevent accidents. Similarly, stock markets have daily price limits to reduce panic buying and panic selling.
An Upper Circuit is the maximum price a stock can rise in a day, while a Lower Circuit is the maximum it can fall.
If a stock has a 10% Upper Circuit and closed yesterday at ₹100, it cannot trade above ₹110 today.
Circuits protect investors from sudden extreme price movements.
